question: Which of the following is the second largest habitat of the One-Horned Rhinoceros in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaldapara National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jaldapara National Park**, located in the state of **West Bengal**, is the second largest habitat of the **One-Horned Rhinoceros** in India.
 
• The park has a rich biodiversity and is known for its **grasslands and forests**, which provide a suitable environment for the One-Horned Rhinoceros to thrive.
 
• It is home to a significant population of this species, second only to **Kaziranga National Park** in Assam.
 
• **Jaldapara** was declared a wildlife sanctuary in **1941** and upgraded to a national park in **2012** for better protection and conservation of its unique wildlife.
 
• The park is situated on the banks of the **Torsa River**, which enhances its ecological diversity and supports various species of flora and fauna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kaziranga National Park:**

 
 
• **Kaziranga National Park**, located in **Assam**, is the largest habitat of the **One-Horned Rhinoceros** in India.
 
• It was declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1985**.
 
• The park is known for its **wetlands, grasslands, and forests**, which support a diverse range of wildlife, including elephants, tigers, and swamp deer.
 
• It hosts more than **2,400 One-Horned Rhinoceroses**, making it a critical area for their conservation.
 
 
 
• **Gir National Park:**
 
 
• **Gir National Park**, located in **Gujarat**, is primarily known as the habitat of **Asiatic Lions** rather than One-Horned Rhinoceroses.
 
• It was established in **1965**, and its unique dry deciduous forest ecosystem supports a variety of wildlife.
 
• Gir does not host any population of One-Horned Rhinoceroses.
 
 
 
• **Kanha National Park:**
 
 
• **Kanha National Park**, located in **Madhya Pradesh**, is renowned for its population of **Royal Bengal Tigers** and **Barasingha** (Swamp Deer).
 
• It does not provide a habitat for the One-Horned Rhinoceros.
 
• Established in **1955**, it is one of the most well-maintained parks in India.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Status:**
 
 
• The **One-Horned Rhinoceros** is classified as a **Vulnerable species** under the **IUCN Red List**.
 
• Efforts like the **Indian Rhino Vision 2020** aim to increase the population of rhinos across protected areas in Assam and West Bengal.
 
• Anti-poaching measures and habitat conservation are critical for their survival.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Protection Efforts:**

 
 
• The One-Horned Rhinoceros was once widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Due to habitat loss and poaching, its range has been reduced to specific protected areas.
 
 
 
• **Tourism and Awareness:**
 
 
• National parks like **Jaldapara** and **Kaziranga** attract tourists, raising awareness about rhino conservation.
 
• Eco-tourism initiatives help generate funds for conservation while engaging local communities.
